title: Per-Issue Status Record
description: Compact committed record at agent-runtime/artifacts/status/issue-<N>.json (#670 P1 Option A). Replaces in-tree verbose review/validation bodies as the wave->main artifact-gate read path; verbose bodies move to CI artifact retention with sha256 integrity references recorded here.

wave.description: waveId this issue was merged under, when known (e.g. 'wave-658'); null when not yet assigned or unknown at migration time.

artifactRef.description: Locator for the verbose review body. Two schemes are admissible. "local-only:<repo-relative-path>" (#1497) is the scheme for the five artifact body directories .gitignore forbids committing (ADR-003: emit is not commit); it claims the body existed on the machine that ran the loop with the recorded sha256, and explicitly NOT that it can be read back — it is admissible only for a path inside those directories, so it cannot launder a dangling reference into a pass. "git-history:<repo-relative-path>" claims the content IS retrievable from history and is checked strictly from gateVersion 2 on (#1445): if it does not resolve to content matching the sha256, the record fails. Records written before #1497 carry git-history: for agent-runtime/artifacts/reviews/ paths, which is the contradiction #1497 fixed.

signoffRequired.description: #1141: true when the review is PASS_WITH_WARNINGS and therefore needs the dual signoff. Optional for backward compatibility with records written before #1141; absent reads as false.

warningsAcknowledged.description: #1141: every gating WARNING finding carries reviewer acceptance plus owner ack. Derived by generate_status_records.py from the same common helper check_findings_acknowledged.py uses; absent reads as false, keeping the retention guard (and the wave-tier gate, #1170) fail-closed.

ownerSignoffPresent.description: #1141: a timestamped owner signoff with acknowledged=true is present on the review body. Derived from the same common helper check_owner_signoff.py uses; absent reads as false.

artifactRef.description: Locator for the verbose validation body. Two schemes are admissible. "local-only:<repo-relative-path>" (#1497) is the scheme for the five artifact body directories .gitignore forbids committing (ADR-003: emit is not commit); it claims the body existed on the machine that ran the loop with the recorded sha256, and explicitly NOT that it can be read back — it is admissible only for a path inside those directories, so it cannot launder a dangling reference into a pass. "git-history:<repo-relative-path>" claims the content IS retrievable from history and is checked strictly from gateVersion 2 on (#1445): if it does not resolve to content matching the sha256, the record fails. Records written before #1497 carry git-history: for agent-runtime/artifacts/validation/ paths, which is the contradiction #1497 fixed.

architecturalChange.description: #1562: the typed answer to 'was this an architectural change?', derived by generate_status_records.py from the review body's two interface limbs and carried here because agent-runtime/artifacts/status/ is the ONLY artifact directory .gitignore keeps tracked — the review body itself never reaches CI (ADR-003: emit is not commit), so check_adr's rung 3 has nothing else to read. It replaces metrics.criticalFindings, which rung 3 used as a proxy: an unfiltered count of findings of every type and severity, non-zero on 109 of the 316 committed records with a guard-admitted review status, and therefore a demand for an ADR on a third of ordinary PRs. Deliberately OPTIONAL and additive, with NO gateVersion bump: absence is self-describing (a reader treats it as 'this source cannot answer' and falls through to fail-closed, never to 'no'), so the ~317 gateVersion 1 and 2 records already on main stay valid, unmodified and un-backfilled, and every existing reader stays correct. Bumping gateVersion would instead have disabled two behaviours keyed on the literal value 2 — check_artifact_retention_guard._ref_verdict's artifactRef integrity check and generate_status_records.relabel_policy_local_refs. The map.md diff limb of architectural_change_detected is deliberately NOT folded in here: the generator has no diff, and check_adr sees that limb directly and conclusively at rung 1, ahead of this record.

value.description: True when at least one named signal fired. The invariant `value === (signals.length > 0)` is what makes this harder to fake than the count it replaces, and check_adr enforces it on read: a record breaking it is refused in BOTH directions rather than half-trusted.

signals.description: Which limb of the review body fired, so the verdict is auditable from the record alone. Closed enum: a boolean re-derived from something that is not an interface signal (metrics.criticalFindings, say) cannot name a member here, so it cannot claim value:true.

criticalFindings.description: len(review.criticalFindings) — an unfiltered count of findings of every type and severity. A volume measure, and NOT a signal that an interface moved: #1562 removed its use as check_adr's architectural-change proxy, where it false-positived on 109 of 316 records. Use architecturalChange for that question.

run.description: #1438, gateVersion 2: harness-captured evidence — what the run was observed to do, as opposed to what the agent typed. One named block per capture provider registered under agent-runtime/scripts/ci/capture_providers/. Deliberately OPEN (no additionalProperties: false) so a new provider ships as one new module and needs no edit to this schema nor to generate_status_records.py; each provider owns the shape of its own block. Absent on gateVersion 1 records — the pre-#1438 records are not backfilled (they record nothing about their runs and never will).

gateVersion.description: Status-record schema/gate-semantics version; bump when the read-path contract changes. 1 = the #670 compact record. 2 = #1438, which adds the run{} capture envelope. Both are readable: v1 records stay valid unchanged and are never backfilled. Enumerated rather than open-ended so a record written by a future generator this reader was not built against fails closed instead of being read on a guess.
